records.arabic: حدثنا الحميدي عبد الله بن الزبير قال حدثنا سفيان قال حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد الأنصاري قال أخبرني محمد بن إبراهيم التيمي أنه سمع علقمة بن وقاص الليثي يقول سمعت عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه على المنبر قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول إنما الأعمال بالنيات وإنما لكل امرئ ما نوى فمن كانت هجرته إلى دنيا يصيبها أو إلى امرأة ينكحها فهجرته إلى ما هاجر إليه
records.english: al-Humaydi Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Said al-Ansari related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi informed me that he heard Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi say: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه, on the pulpit, say: I heard the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم say: "Deeds depend only on intentions, and each person has only what he intended. Whoever's migration was for worldly gain he would obtain, or a woman he would marry, his migration is to what he migrated to."

records.arabic: حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال أخبرنا مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أم المؤمنين رضي الله عنها أن الحارث بن هشام رضي الله عنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا رسول الله كيف يأتيك الوحي فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أحيانا يأتيني مثل صلصلة الجرس وهو أشده علي فيفصم عني وقد وعيت عنه ما قال وأحيانا يتمثل لي الملك رجلا فيكلمني فأعي ما يقول قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها ولقد رأيته ينزل عليه الوحي في اليوم الشديد البرد فيفصم عنه وإن جبينه ليتفصد عرقا
records.english: Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us, saying: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aishah, Mother of the Believers, رضي الله عنها, that al-Harith ibn Hisham رضي الله عنه asked the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم: "Messenger of God, how does revelation come to you?" The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said: "Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and that is the hardest for me. It then lifts from me, and I have grasped what he said. Sometimes the angel takes the form of a man for me and speaks to me, and I grasp what he says." Aishah رضي الله عنها said: "I have indeed seen revelation descend upon him on a bitterly cold day, then lift from him while sweat poured from his forehead."

segments.arabic: حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال أخبرنا مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أم المؤمنين رضي الله عنها

أن الحارث بن هشام رضي الله عنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا رسول الله كيف يأتيك الوحي فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أحيانا يأتيني مثل صلصلة الجرس وهو أشده علي فيفصم عني وقد وعيت عنه ما قال وأحيانا يتمثل لي الملك رجلا فيكلمني فأعي ما يقول قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها ولقد رأيته ينزل عليه الوحي في اليوم الشديد البرد فيفصم عنه وإن جبينه ليتفصد عرقا

records.arabic: حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن بن شهاب عن عروة بن الزبير عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة في النوم فكان لا يرى رؤيا إلا جاءت مثل فلق الصبح ثم حبب إليه الخلاء وكان يخلو بغار حراء فيتحنث فيه وهو التعبد الليالي ذوات العدد قبل أن ينزع إلى أهله ويتزود لذلك ثم يرجع إلى خديجة فيتزود لمثلها حتى جاءه الحق وهو في غار حراء فجاءه الملك فقال اقرأ قال ما أنا بقارئ قال فأخذني فغطني حتى بلغ مني الجهد ثم أرسلني فقال اقرأ قلت ما أنا بقارئ فأخذني فغطني الثانية حتى بلغ مني الجهد ثم أرسلني فقال اقرأ فقلت ما أنا بقارئ فأخذني فغطني الثالثة ثم أرسلني فقال اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق خلق الإنسان من علق اقرأ وربك الأكرم فرجع بها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يرجف فؤاده فدخل على خديجة بنت خويلد رضي الله عنها فقال زملوني زملوني فزملوه حتى ذهب عنه الروع فقال لخديجة وأخبرها الخبر لقد خشيت على نفسي فقالت خديجة كلا والله ما يخزيك الله أبدا إنك لتصل الرحم وتحمل الكل وتكسب المعدوم وتقري الضيف وتعين على نوائب الحق فانطلقت به خديجة حتى أتت به ورقة بن نوفل بن أسد بن عبد العزى بن عم خديجة وكان امرأ تنصر في الجاهلية وكان يكتب الكتاب العبراني فيكتب من الإنجيل بالعبرانية ما شاء الله أن يكتب وكان شيخا كبيرا قد عمي فقالت له خديجة يا بن عم اسمع من بن أخيك فقال له ورقة يا بن أخي ماذا ترى فأخبره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خبر ما رأى فقال له ورقة هذا الناموس الذي نزل الله على موسى يا ليتني فيها جذع ليتني أكون حيا إذ يخرجك قومك فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو مخرجي هم قال نعم لم يأت رجل قط بمثل ما جئت به إلا عودي وإن يدركني يومك أنصرك نصرا مؤزرا ثم لم ينشب ورقة أن توفي وفتر الوحي
records.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us, saying: al-Layth related to us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Aishah, Mother of the Believers, that she said: The first revelation with which the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم began was the good dream during sleep. No dream he saw failed to come like the breaking of morning. Then solitude was made dear to him. He would withdraw to the cave of Hira and practice devotion there, that is, worship, for a number of nights before returning to his household, taking provisions for this. Then he would return to Khadijah and take provisions for another such period, until the truth came to him while he was in the cave of Hira. The angel came to him and said, "Read." He said, "I am not a reader." He said: "He seized me and pressed me until I reached the limit of endurance, then released me and said, 'Read.' I said, 'I am not a reader.' He seized me and pressed me a second time until I reached the limit of endurance, then released me and said, 'Read.' I said, 'I am not a reader.' He seized me and pressed me a third time, then released me and said, 'Read in the name of your Lord who created, created the human being from a clinging clot. Read, and your Lord is the most generous.'" The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم returned with these words, his heart trembling. He went in to Khadijah bint Khuwaylid رضي الله عنها and said, "Wrap me up, wrap me up." They wrapped him up until his terror passed. He told Khadijah what had happened and said to her, "I have feared for myself." Khadijah said: "No! By God, God will never disgrace you. You maintain kinship ties, bear the burdens of those unable to bear them, earn for the destitute, entertain the guest, and help with afflictions that call for rightful aid." Khadijah went with him until she brought him to Waraqah ibn Nawfal ibn Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza, Khadijah's paternal cousin. He was a man who had become Christian in the time of ignorance. He used to write the Hebrew script, writing from the Gospel in Hebrew whatever God willed that he write. He was an elderly man who had become blind. Khadijah said to him, "Cousin, listen to your brother's son." Waraqah said to him, "My brother's son, what do you see?" The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم told him what he had seen. Waraqah said to him: "This is the bearer of the secret whom God sent down to Musa. If only I were a vigorous young man during it! If only I were alive when your people drive you out!" The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said, "Will they really drive me out?" He said: "Yes. No man has ever brought anything like what you have brought without being met with hostility. If your day reaches me, I shall give you forceful support." Soon afterward Waraqah died, and revelation paused.

records.arabic: قال بن شهاب وأخبرني أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن أن جابر بن عبد الله الأنصاري قال وهو يحدث عن فترة الوحي فقال في حديثه بينا أنا أمشي إذ سمعت صوتا من السماء فرفعت بصري فإذا الملك الذي جاءني بحراء جالس على كرسي بين السماء والأرض فرعبت منه فرجعت فقلت زملوني زملوني فأنزل الله تعالى يا أيها المدثر قم فأنذر إلى قوله والرجز فاهجر فحمي الوحي وتتابع تابعه عبد الله بن يوسف وأبو صالح وتابعه هلال بن رداد عن الزهري وقال يونس ومعمر بوادره
records.english: Ibn Shihab said: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman also informed me that Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari said, while relating the pause in revelation, in his account: [The following first-person account is the Messenger's:] "As I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my eyes, and there was the angel who had come to me at Hira, sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I was terrified of him and returned, saying, 'Wrap me up, wrap me up.' Then God تعالى sent down, 'You who are wrapped in a cloak, rise and warn,' through His words, 'And shun defilement.' Revelation then grew intense and came in succession." Abdullah ibn Yusuf and Abu Salih followed him in transmitting it; Hilal ibn Raddad also followed him, from al-Zuhri. Yunus and Mamar said, "his upper chest muscles" [an isolated variant phrase in the source].

records.arabic: حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال حدثنا أبو عوانة قال حدثنا موسى بن أبي عائشة قال حدثنا سعيد بن جبير عن بن عباس في قوله تعالى لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعالج من التنزيل شدة وكان مما يحرك شفتيه فقال بن عباس فأنا أحركهما لكم كما كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يحركهما وقال سعيد أنا أحركهما كما رأيت بن عباس يحركهما فحرك شفتيه فأنزل الله تعالى لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه قال جمعه له في صدرك وتقرأه فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه قال فاستمع له وأنصت ثم إن علينا بيانه ثم إن علينا أن تقرأه فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد ذلك إذا أتاه جبريل استمع فإذا انطلق جبريل قرأه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كما قرأه
records.english: Musa ibn Ismail related to us, saying: Abu Awanah related to us, saying: Musa ibn Abi Aishah related to us, saying: Said ibn Jubayr related to us, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words تعالى, "Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it." He said: The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم used to struggle with the severity of revelation, and among what he did was to move his lips. Ibn Abbas said, "I shall move them for you as the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم used to move them." Said said, "I move them as I saw Ibn Abbas move them." He moved his lips. Then God تعالى sent down, "Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Its gathering and its recitation are Our responsibility." He said: "Gathering it for him in your breast, and that you recite it. [The source has third-person “for him” alongside second-person “your breast” and “you recite it”; the intended pronoun remains uncertain.]" "So when We recite it, follow its recitation." He said: "Listen to it and keep silent." "Then its explanation is Our responsibility." [Explanatory gloss:] “Then it is Our responsibility that you recite it.” After that, when Jibril came to the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم, he listened, and when Jibril departed, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم recited it as he had recited it.

records.arabic: حدثنا عبدان قال أخبرنا عبد الله قال أخبرنا يونس عن الزهري ح وحدثنا بشر بن محمد قال أخبرنا عبد الله قال أخبرنا يونس ومعمر عن الزهري نحوه قال أخبرني عبيد الله بن عبد الله عن بن عباس قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أجود الناس وكان أجود ما يكون في رمضان حين يلقاه جبريل وكان يلقاه في كل ليلة من رمضان فيدارسه القرآن فلرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أجود بالخير من الريح المرسلة
records.english: Abdan related to us, saying: Abdullah informed us, saying: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri. [Change of chain.] Bishr ibn Muhammad also related to us, saying: Abdullah informed us, saying: Yunus and Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri, similarly. He said: Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah informed me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم was the most generous of people, and he was at his most generous in Ramadan when Jibril met him. He would meet him every night of Ramadan and study the Quran together with him. The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم was indeed more generous with good than the wind sent forth.

records.arabic: حدثنا أبو اليمان الحكم بن نافع قال أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال أخبرني عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة بن مسعود أن عبد الله بن عباس أخبره أن أبا سفيان بن حرب أخبره أن هرقل أرسل إليه في ركب من قريش وكانوا تجارا بالشام في المدة التي كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ماد فيها أبا سفيان وكفار قريش فأتوه وهم بإيلياء فدعاهم في مجلسه وحوله عظماء الروم ثم دعاهم ودعا بترجمانه فقال أيكم أقرب نسبا بهذا الرجل الذي يزعم أنه نبي فقال أبو سفيان فقلت أنا أقربهم نسبا فقال أدنوه مني وقربوا أصحابه فاجعلوهم عند ظهره ثم قال لترجمانه قل لهم إني سائل هذا عن هذا الرجل فإن كذبني فكذبوه فوالله لولا الحياء من أن يأثروا علي كذبا لكذبت عنه ثم كان أول ما سألني عنه أن قال كيف نسبه فيكم قلت هو فينا ذو نسب قال فهل قال هذا القول منكم أحد قط قبله قلت لا قال فهل كان من آبائه من ملك قلت لا قال فأشراف الناس يتبعونه أم ضعفاؤهم فقلت بل ضعفاؤهم قال أيزيدون أم ينقصون قلت بل يزيدون قال فهل يرتد أحد منهم سخطة لدينه بعد أن يدخل فيه قلت لا قال فهل كنتم تتهمونه بالكذب قبل أن يقول ما قال قلت لا قال فهل يغدر قلت لا ونحن منه في مدة لا ندري ما هو فاعل فيها قال ولم تمكني كلمة أدخل فيها شيئا غير هذه الكلمة قال فهل قاتلتموه قلت نعم قال فكيف كان قتالكم إياه قلت الحرب بيننا وبينه سجال ينال منا وننال منه قال ماذا يأمركم قلت يقول اعبدوا الله وحده ولا تشركوا به شيئا واتركوا ما يقول آباؤكم ويأمرنا بالصلاة والصدق والعفاف والصلة فقال للترجمان قل له سألتك عن نسبه فذكرت أنه فيكم ذو نسب فكذلك الرسل تبعث في نسب قومها وسألتك هل قال أحد منكم هذا القول فذكرت أن لا فقلت لو كان أحد قال هذا القول قبله لقلت رجل يأتسي بقول قيل قبله وسألتك هل كان من آبائه من ملك فذكرت أن لا قلت فلو كان من آبائه من ملك قلت رجل يطلب ملك أبيه وسألتك هل كنتم تتهمونه بالكذب قبل أن يقول ما قال فذكرت أن لا فقد أعرف أنه لم يكن ليذر الكذب على الناس ويكذب على الله وسألتك أشراف الناس اتبعوه أم ضعفاؤهم فذكرت أن ضعفاءهم اتبعوه وهم أتباع الرسل وسألتك أيزيدون أم ينقصون فذكرت أنهم يزيدون وكذلك أمر الإيمان حتى يتم وسألتك أيرتد أحد سخطة لدينه بعد أن يدخل فيه فذكرت أن لا وكذلك الإيمان حين تخالط بشاشته القلوب وسألتك هل يغدر فذكرت أن لا وكذلك الرسل لا تغدر وسألتك بما يأمركم فذكرت أنه يأمركم أن تعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئا وينهاكم عن عبادة الأوثان ويأمركم بالصلاة والصدق والعفاف فإن كان ما تقول حقا فسيملك موضع قدمي هاتين وقد كنت أعلم أنه خارج لم أكن أظن أنه منكم فلو أني أعلم أني أخلص إليه لتجشمت لقاءه ولو كنت عنده لغسلت عن قدمه ثم دعا بكتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الذي بعث به دحية إلى عظيم بصرى فدفعه إلى هرقل فقرأه فإذا فيه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم من محمد عبد الله ورسوله إلى هرقل عظيم الروم سلام على من اتبع الهدى أما بعد فإني أدعوك بدعاية الإسلام أسلم تسلم يؤتك الله أجرك مرتين فإن توليت فإن عليك إثم الأريسيين قل يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم ألا نعبد إلا الله ولا نشرك به شيئا ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله فإن تولوا فقولوا اشهدوا بأنا مسلمون يا قال أبو سفيان فلما قال ما قال وفرغ من قراءة الكتاب كثر عنده الصخب وارتفعت الأصوات وأخرجنا فقلت لأصحابي حين أخرجنا لقد أمر أمر بن أبي كبشة إنه يخافه ملك بني الأصفر فما زلت موقنا أنه سيظهر حتى أدخل الله علي الإسلام وكان بن الناظور صاحب إيلياء وهرقل أسقفا على نصارى الشام يحدث أن هرقل حين قدم إيلياء أصبح يوما خبيث النفس فقال بعض بطارقته قد استنكرنا هيئتك قال بن الناظور وكان هرقل حزاء ينظر في النجوم فقال لهم حين سألوه إني رأيت الليلة حين نظرت في النجوم ملك الختان قد ظهر فمن يختتن من هذه الأمة قالوا ليس يختتن إلا اليهود فلا يهمنك شأنهم واكتب إلى مداين ملكك فيقتلوا من فيهم من اليهود فبينما هم على أمرهم أتي هرقل برجل أرسل به ملك غسان يخبر عن خبر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما استخبره هرقل قال اذهبوا فانظروا أمختتن هو أم لا فنظروا إليه فحدثوه أنه مختتن وسأله عن العرب فقال هم يختتنون فقال هرقل هذا ملك هذه الأمة قد ظهر ثم كتب هرقل إلى صاحب له برومية وكان نظيره في العلم وسار هرقل إلى حمص فلم يرم حمص حتى أتاه كتاب من صاحبه يوافق رأي هرقل على خروج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنه نبي فأذن هرقل لعظماء الروم في دسكرة له بحمص ثم أمر بأبوابها فغلقت ثم اطلع فقال يا معشر الروم هل لكم في الفلاح والرشد وأن يثبت ملككم فتبايعوا هذا النبي فحاصوا حيصة حمر الوحش إلى الأبواب فوجدوها قد غلقت فلما رأى هرقل نفرتهم وأيس من الإيمان قال ردوهم علي وقال إني قلت مقالتي آنفا أختبر بها شدتكم على دينكم فقد رأيت فسجدوا له ورضوا عنه فكان ذلك آخر شأن هرقل رواه صالح بن كيسان ويونس ومعمر عن الزهري بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
records.english:
Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi related to us, saying: Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Masud informed me that Abdullah ibn Abbas informed him that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb informed him that Heraclius sent for him among a riding party of Quraysh. They were merchants in al-Sham during the period in which the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم had made a truce with Abu Sufyan and the unbelievers of Quraysh. They came to him while they were at Iliya. He summoned them to his assembly, with the grandees of the Romans around him. Then he summoned them and his interpreter and said, "Which of you is closest in kinship to this man who claims to be a prophet?" Abu Sufyan said: I said, "I am the closest of them in kinship." He said, "Bring him close to me, and bring his companions near and place them behind him." Then he said to his interpreter, "Tell them: I shall ask this man about that man. If he lies to me, contradict him." By God, had I not been ashamed that they would recount a lie against me, I would have lied about him. The first thing he asked me was, "What is his lineage among you?" I said, "Among us he has an established lineage." He said, "Has anyone among you ever said this before him?" I said, "No." He said, "Was any of his forefathers a king?" I said, "No." He said, "Do the prominent people follow him or their weak?" I said, "Rather, their weak." He said, "Are they increasing or decreasing?" I said, "Rather, increasing." He said, "Does any of them turn back out of displeasure with his religion after entering it?" I said, "No." He said, "Did you accuse him of lying before he said what he has said?" I said, "No." He said, "Does he betray?" I said, "No. We are in a period of truce with him and do not know what he will do during it." He said: No remark allowed me to insert anything except this one. He said, "Have you fought him?" I said, "Yes." He said, "How has your fighting with him gone?" I said, "The war between us and him takes turns: he gains against us and we gain against him." He said, "What does he command you?" I said: "He says, 'Worship God alone and associate nothing with Him, and leave what your forefathers say.' He commands us to pray, to be truthful and chaste, and to maintain ties."
He said to the interpreter: "Tell him: I asked you about his lineage, and you said that among you he has an established lineage. Thus the messengers are sent within the lineage of their people. I asked you whether anyone among you had said this, and you said no. I said to myself: If anyone had said this before him, I would have said he was a man following something said before him. I asked you whether any of his forefathers was a king, and you said no. I said: Had any of his forefathers been a king, I would have said he was a man seeking his father's kingship. I asked you whether you accused him of lying before he said what he has said, and you said no. I thus recognize that he would not leave off lying about people and lie about God. I asked you whether prominent people or their weak followed him, and you said their weak followed him. They are the followers of the messengers. I asked you whether they were increasing or decreasing, and you said they were increasing. Such is the course of faith until it becomes complete. I asked you whether anyone turns back out of displeasure with his religion after entering it, and you said no. Such is faith when its delight mingles with hearts. I asked you whether he betrays, and you said no. Likewise the messengers do not betray. I asked you what he commands you, and you said he commands you to worship God and associate nothing with Him, forbids you to worship idols, and commands you to pray, to be truthful and chaste. If what you say is true, he will possess the place of these two feet of mine. I knew that he was to come forth; I did not think he was from among you. If I knew that I could reach him, I would undertake the difficulty of meeting him. If I were with him, I would wash his foot."
Then he called for the letter of the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم, which he had sent with Dihyah to the grandee of Busra, who handed it on to Heraclius. He read it, and it contained: "بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم. From Muhammad, God's servant and His messenger, to Heraclius, grandee of the Romans. سلام على من اتبع الهدى. To proceed: I call you with the call of Islam. Enter Islam and you will be safe; God will give you your reward twice. If you turn away, the sin of the arisiyyin [the designation is uncertain in this source] rests on you. Say: O you, the People of the Book, come to a word shared equally between us and you: that we worship only God, associate nothing with Him, and none of us take others as lords apart from God. If they turn away, say: Bear witness that we submit." [The source then has the isolated address particle "O".] Abu Sufyan said: When he had said what he said and finished reading the letter, there was much clamor around him, voices rose, and we were sent out. When we were sent out, I said to my companions, "The affair of the son of Abu Kabsha has indeed grown great: the king of Banu al-Asfar fears him." I remained certain that he would prevail until God brought Islam upon me.
Ibn al-Natur, the associate of Iliya and Heraclius, a bishop over the Christians of al-Sham, used to relate that when Heraclius came to Iliya, he was one morning in a foul mood. Some of his patricians said, "We find your appearance unusual." Ibn al-Natur said: Heraclius was a diviner who studied the stars. When they questioned him, he said, "Tonight, when I looked at the stars, I saw that the kingship of circumcision had appeared. Who among this people practices circumcision?" They said, "Only the Jews practice circumcision. Do not let their affair concern you. Write to the cities of your kingdom, and let them kill the Jews in them." While they were engaged in their affair, a man sent by the king of Ghassan was brought to Heraclius to report news of the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم. When Heraclius had questioned him, he said, "Go and see whether he is circumcised or not." They examined him and told him he was circumcised. He asked him about the Arabs, and he said, "They practice circumcision." Heraclius said, "This is the kingship of this people: it has appeared." Then Heraclius wrote to a companion of his in Rumiyah who was his equal in knowledge, and Heraclius traveled to Hims. He had not left Hims when a letter from his companion reached him agreeing with Heraclius's view concerning the emergence of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and that he was a prophet. Heraclius then admitted the grandees of the Romans to an enclosed estate of his in Hims, and ordered its doors shut. Then he appeared and said, "People of the Romans, would you have success and right direction, and have your kingship endure? Then pledge allegiance to this prophet." They bolted like wild asses toward the doors and found them shut. When Heraclius saw their aversion and despaired of faith, he said, "Bring them back to me." He said, "What I said just now was to test your firmness in your religion, and I have seen it." They prostrated themselves before him and were pleased with him. That was the last of Heraclius's affair. Salih ibn Kaysan, Yunus, and Mamar related it from al-Zuhri. بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم [This final invocation occurs here in the frozen source unit after the transmission notice; whether it belongs to this material or opens following material is uncertain.]

segments.arabic: حدثنا أبو اليمان الحكم بن نافع قال أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال أخبرني عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة بن مسعود أن عبد الله بن عباس أخبره أن أبا سفيان بن حرب أخبره

أن هرقل أرسل إليه في ركب من قريش وكانوا تجارا بالشام في المدة التي كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ماد فيها أبا سفيان وكفار قريش فأتوه وهم بإيلياء فدعاهم في مجلسه وحوله عظماء الروم ثم دعاهم ودعا بترجمانه فقال أيكم أقرب نسبا بهذا الرجل الذي يزعم أنه نبي فقال أبو سفيان فقلت أنا أقربهم نسبا فقال أدنوه مني وقربوا أصحابه فاجعلوهم عند ظهره ثم قال لترجمانه قل لهم إني سائل هذا عن هذا الرجل فإن كذبني فكذبوه فوالله لولا الحياء من أن يأثروا علي كذبا لكذبت عنه ثم كان أول ما سألني عنه أن قال كيف نسبه فيكم قلت هو فينا ذو نسب قال فهل قال هذا القول منكم أحد قط قبله قلت لا قال فهل كان من آبائه من ملك قلت لا قال فأشراف الناس يتبعونه أم ضعفاؤهم فقلت بل ضعفاؤهم قال أيزيدون أم ينقصون قلت بل يزيدون قال فهل يرتد أحد منهم سخطة لدينه بعد أن يدخل فيه قلت لا قال فهل كنتم تتهمونه بالكذب قبل أن يقول ما قال قلت لا قال فهل يغدر قلت لا ونحن منه في مدة لا ندري ما هو فاعل فيها قال ولم تمكني كلمة أدخل فيها شيئا غير هذه الكلمة قال فهل قاتلتموه قلت نعم قال فكيف كان قتالكم إياه قلت الحرب بيننا وبينه سجال ينال منا وننال منه قال ماذا يأمركم قلت يقول اعبدوا الله وحده ولا تشركوا به شيئا واتركوا ما يقول آباؤكم ويأمرنا بالصلاة والصدق والعفاف والصلة فقال للترجمان قل له سألتك عن نسبه فذكرت أنه فيكم ذو نسب فكذلك الرسل تبعث في نسب قومها وسألتك هل قال أحد منكم هذا القول فذكرت أن لا فقلت لو كان أحد قال هذا القول قبله لقلت رجل يأتسي بقول قيل قبله وسألتك هل كان من آبائه من ملك فذكرت أن لا قلت فلو كان من آبائه من ملك قلت رجل يطلب ملك أبيه وسألتك هل كنتم تتهمونه بالكذب قبل أن يقول ما قال فذكرت أن لا فقد أعرف أنه لم يكن ليذر الكذب على الناس ويكذب على الله وسألتك أشراف الناس اتبعوه أم ضعفاؤهم فذكرت أن ضعفاءهم اتبعوه وهم أتباع الرسل وسألتك أيزيدون أم ينقصون فذكرت أنهم يزيدون وكذلك أمر الإيمان حتى يتم وسألتك أيرتد أحد سخطة لدينه بعد أن يدخل فيه فذكرت أن لا وكذلك الإيمان حين تخالط بشاشته القلوب وسألتك هل يغدر فذكرت أن لا وكذلك الرسل لا تغدر وسألتك بما يأمركم فذكرت أنه يأمركم أن تعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئا وينهاكم عن عبادة الأوثان ويأمركم بالصلاة والصدق والعفاف فإن كان ما تقول حقا فسيملك موضع قدمي هاتين وقد كنت أعلم أنه خارج لم أكن أظن أنه منكم فلو أني أعلم أني أخلص إليه لتجشمت لقاءه ولو كنت عنده لغسلت عن قدمه ثم دعا بكتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الذي بعث به دحية إلى عظيم بصرى فدفعه إلى هرقل فقرأه فإذا فيه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم من محمد عبد الله ورسوله إلى هرقل عظيم الروم سلام على من اتبع الهدى أما بعد فإني أدعوك بدعاية الإسلام أسلم تسلم يؤتك الله أجرك مرتين فإن توليت فإن عليك إثم الأريسيين قل يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم ألا نعبد إلا الله ولا نشرك به شيئا ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله فإن تولوا فقولوا اشهدوا بأنا مسلمون
يا

قال أبو سفيان فلما قال ما قال وفرغ من قراءة الكتاب كثر عنده الصخب وارتفعت الأصوات وأخرجنا فقلت لأصحابي حين أخرجنا لقد أمر أمر بن أبي كبشة إنه يخافه ملك بني الأصفر فما زلت موقنا أنه سيظهر حتى أدخل الله علي الإسلام

Salih, Yunus, and Mamar are parallel suspended supports from al-Zuhri, with no fabricated suffix or settled referent. The isolated يا at 2703:2705 and the final basmalah boundary remain visible. records.arabic: وهو قول وفعل ويزيد وينقص قال الله تعالى ليزدادوا إيمانا مع إيمانهم وزدناهم هدى ويزيد الله الذين اهتدوا هدى والذين اهتدوا زادهم هدى وآتاهم تقواهم ويزداد الذين آمنوا إيمانا وقوله أيكم زادته هذه إيمانا فأما الذين آمنوا فزادتهم إيمانا وقوله جل ذكره فاخشوهم فزادهم إيمانا وقوله تعالى وما زادهم إلا إيمانا وتسليما والحب في الله والبغض في الله من الإيمان وكتب عمر بن عبد العزيز إلى عدي بن عدي إن للإيمان فرائض وشرائع وحدودا وسننا فمن استكملها استكمل الإيمان ومن لم يستكملها لم يستكمل الإيمان فإن أعش فسأبينها لكم حتى تعملوا بها وإن أمت فما أنا على صحبتكم بحريص وقال إبراهيم عليه السلام ولكن ليطمئن قلبي وقال معاذ اجلس بنا نؤمن ساعة وقال بن مسعود اليقين الإيمان كله وقال بن عمر لا يبلغ العبد حقيقة التقوى حتى يدع ما حاك في الصدر وقال مجاهد شرع لكم أوصيناك يا محمد وإياه دينا واحدا وقال بن عباس شرعة ومنهاجا سبيلا وسنة دعاؤكم إيمانكم لقوله عز وجل قل ما يعبأ بكم ربي لولا دعاؤكم ومعنى الدعاء في اللغة الإيمان )
records.english: Faith is speech and action; it increases and decreases. God تعالى said, “That they may increase in faith along with their faith”; “We increased them in guidance”; “God increases in guidance those who have been guided”; “Those who have been guided—He increased them in guidance and gave them their reverence”; and “That those who believe may increase in faith.” And His statement: “Which of you has this increased in faith? As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith.” And His statement, جل ذكره: “So fear them”; “But it increased them in faith.” And His statement, تعالى: “It increased them only in faith and submission.” Loving for God and hating for God are part of faith. Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz wrote to Adi ibn Adi: “Faith has obligations, prescribed ways, limits, and established practices. Whoever completes them has completed faith, and whoever does not complete them has not completed faith. If I live, I shall explain them to you so that you may act on them. If I die, I am not eager to keep your company.” Ibrahim عليه السلام said, “But so that my heart may be reassured.” Muadh said, “Sit with us; let us have faith for a while.” Ibn Masud said, “Certainty is the whole of faith.” Ibn Umar said, “A servant does not attain the reality of reverence until he leaves what troubles his breast.” Mujahid said concerning “He prescribed for you”: “We enjoined upon you, Muhammad, and upon him one religion.” Ibn Abbas said concerning “a prescribed way and a path”: “A way and an established practice.” “Your supplication” means “your faith,” on account of His statement, عز وجل: “Say: What concern would my Lord have for you were it not for your supplication?” The meaning of supplication in the language is faith.)

Muadh is named as speaker of the invitation to believe for a while. No compiler-to-Muadh chain is printed; neither a fuller personal identity nor missing transmitters can be established from this saying.
Ibn Masud is credited with the certainty maxim without a printed transmission route. The gap reflects absence of the route, not a claim about how many people transmitted it.
Ibn Umar is credited with the statement about leaving what troubles the breast. Attribution is preserved, but the excerpt supplies no chain to him and does not establish historical contact.
Mujahid supplies the gloss on prescribed religion without a chain from the compiler. Muhammad and the other person addressed inside the gloss are quoted subjects, not additional transmission nodes.

The explicit Ibn Abbas attribution introduces the prescribed-way/path gloss. The adjoining unpunctuated دعاؤكم إيمانكم passage has no printed speaker transition: its extent as an Ibn Abbas gloss versus ensuing compiler explanation remains unsettled. The current narrow envelope is an editorial boundary, not proof of a new speaker; the English leaves that next gloss unattributed. The route to Ibn Abbas is also absent.

records.english: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us; he said: Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan informed us, from Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Ibn Umar رضي الله عنهما, who said: The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “Islam was built on five: testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, establishing prayer, giving the obligatory alms, pilgrimage, and fasting Ramadan.”

records.arabic: وقول الله تعالى ليس البر أن تولوا وجوهكم قبل المشرق والمغرب ولكن البر من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر والملائكة والكتاب والنبيين وآتى المال على حبه ذوي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل والسائلين وفي الرقاب وأقام الصلاة وآتى الزكاة والموفون بعهدهم إذا عاهدوا والصابرين في البأساء والضراء وحين البأس أولئك الذين صدقوا وأولئك هم المتقون قد أفلح المؤمنون الآية )
records.english: And the statement of God تعالى: “Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east and the west. Rather, righteousness is in one who believes in God, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets; gives wealth, despite his love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask, and for freeing those in bondage; establishes prayer and gives the obligatory alms; and those who fulfill their covenant when they make a covenant, and those who are patient in hardship, affliction, and the time of battle. Those are the ones who have been true, and those are the reverent.” “The believers have indeed prospered”—the verse.) [The pronoun in “على حبه” does not explicitly name its object: love of the wealth is the reading used here; love of God remains another possible reading.]

records.english: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us; he said: Abu Amir al-Aqadi narrated to us; he said: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, who said, “Faith has sixty-some branches, and modesty is a branch of faith.”

records.arabic: حدثنا آدم بن أبي إياس قال حدثنا شعبة عن عبد الله بن أبي السفر وإسماعيل عن الشعبي عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال المسلم من سلم المسلمون من لسانه ويده والمهاجر من هجر ما نهى الله عنه قال أبو عبد الله وقال أبو معاوية حدثنا داود عن عامر قال سمعت عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال عبد الأعلى عن داود عن عامر عن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم \ 1 \
records.english: Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us; he said: Shubah narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abi al-Safar and Ismail, from al-Shabi, from Abdullah ibn Amr رضي الله عنهما, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, who said, “A Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand Muslims are safe, and an emigrant is one who abandons what God has forbidden.” Abu Abdullah said: Abu Muawiyah also said: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir, who said: I heard Abdullah, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. Abd al-Ala also said: From Dawud, from Amir, from Abdullah, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. [Source layout marker: backslash, 1, backslash.]

segments.arabic: حدثنا آدم بن أبي إياس قال حدثنا شعبة عن عبد الله بن أبي السفر وإسماعيل عن الشعبي عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

records.english: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us; he said: Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us; he said: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, who said, “There are three qualities which, when present in someone, allow him to find the sweetness of faith: that God and His Messenger be dearer to him than anything besides them; that he love a person, loving him only for God; and that he hate to return to unbelief as he hates to be thrown into the Fire.”

records.arabic: حدثنا أبو اليمان قال أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال أخبرني أبو إدريس عائذ الله بن عبد الله أن عبادة بن الصامت رضي الله عنه وكان شهد بدرا وهو أحد النقباء ليلة العقبة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال وحوله عصابة من أصحابه بايعوني على أن لا تشركوا بالله شيئا ولا تسرقوا ولا تزنوا ولا تقتلوا أولادكم ولا تأتوا ببهتان تفترونه بين أيديكم وأرجلكم ولا تعصوا في معروف فمن وفي منكم فأجره على الله ومن أصاب من ذلك شيئا فعوقب في الدنيا فهو كفارة له ومن أصاب من ذلك شيئا ثم ستره الله فهو إلى الله إن شاء عفا عنه وإن شاء عاقبه فبايعناه على ذلك
records.english: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; he said: Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Idris Aidh Allah ibn Abdullah informed me that Ubadah ibn al-Samit رضي الله عنه—who had been present at Badr and was one of the leaders on the night of al-Aqabah—related that the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم, with a group of his companions around him, said, “Pledge to me that you will associate nothing with God, will not steal, will not commit unlawful sexual intercourse, will not kill your children, will not bring a slander you fabricate between your hands and your feet, and will not disobey in anything right. Whoever among you fulfills this, his reward rests with God. Whoever commits any of these things and is punished in this world, that is an expiation for him. Whoever commits any of these things and God then conceals him, his affair rests with God: if He wills, He pardons him; if He wills, He punishes him.” So we pledged to him on that basis.

records.arabic: حدثنا محمد بن سلام قال أخبرنا عبدة عن هشام عن أبيه عن عائشة قالت كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أمرهم أمرهم من الأعمال بما يطيقون قالوا إنا لسنا كهيئتك يا رسول الله إن الله قد غفر لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر فيغضب حتى يعرف الغضب في وجهه ثم يقول إن أتقاكم وأعلمكم بالله أنا \ 1 \
records.english: Muhammad ibn Salam narrated to us; he said: Abdah informed us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aishah, who said: When the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم commanded them, he commanded them to do deeds within their ability. They said, “We are not in your position, Messenger of God. God has forgiven your earlier and later sin.” He would become angry until anger could be seen in his face, then say, “I am indeed the most reverent of you and the one who knows God best.” [Source layout marker: backslash, 1, backslash.]

segments.arabic: حدثنا محمد بن سلام قال أخبرنا عبدة عن هشام عن أبيه عن عائشة

records.english: Ismail narrated to us; he said: Malik narrated to me, from Amr ibn Yahya al-Mazini, from his father, from Abu Said al-Khudri رضي الله عنه, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, who said, “The people of the Garden will enter the Garden, and the people of the Fire the Fire. Then God تعالى will say, ‘Bring out whoever has in his heart a mustard seed's weight of faith.’ They will be brought out of it, having become blackened, and cast into the river of rain—or life [Malik was unsure]. They will grow as a seed grows beside the floodwater. Have you not seen how it emerges yellow and curling?” Wuhayb said: Amr narrated to us, saying “life”; and he said, “a mustard seed of goodness.”

records.arabic: حدثنا محمد بن عبيد الله قال حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد عن صالح عن بن شهاب عن أبي أمامة بن سهل أنه سمع أبا سعيد الخدري يقول قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بينا أنا نائم رأيت الناس يعرضون علي وعليهم قمص منها ما يبلغ الثدي ومنها ما دون ذلك وعرض علي عمر بن الخطاب وعليه قميص يجره قالوا فما أولت ذلك يا رسول الله قال الدين
records.english: Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah narrated to us; he said: Ibrahim ibn Sad narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl, that he heard Abu Said al-Khudri say: The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “While I was asleep, I saw people being presented to me wearing shirts, some reaching the breasts and some shorter than that. Umar ibn al-Khattab was presented to me wearing a shirt that he was dragging.” They said, “How did you interpret that, Messenger of God?” He said, “Religion.”

segments.arabic: حدثنا محمد بن عبيد الله قال حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد عن صالح عن بن شهاب عن أبي أمامة بن سهل أنه سمع أبا سعيد الخدري يقول قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

records.arabic: حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال أخبرنا مالك بن أنس عن بن شهاب عن سالم بن عبد الله عن أبيه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مر على رجل من الأنصار وهو يعظ أخاه في الحياء فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم دعه فإن الحياء من الإيمان
records.english: Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; he said: Malik ibn Anas informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn Abdullah, from his father: The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم passed a man of the Ansar who was admonishing his brother about modesty. The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “Leave him, for modesty is part of faith.”

records.arabic: حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد المسندي قال حدثنا أبو روح الحرمي بن عمارة قال حدثنا شعبة عن واقد بن محمد قال سمعت أبي يحدث عن بن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يشهدوا أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله ويقيموا الصلاة ويؤتوا الزكاة فإذا فعلوا ذلك عصموا مني دماءهم وأموالهم إلا بحق الإسلام وحسابهم على الله
records.english: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Musnadi narrated to us; he said: Abu Rawh al-Harami ibn Umarah narrated to us; he said: Shubah narrated to us, from Waqid ibn Muhammad, who said: I heard my father narrating from Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “I have been commanded to fight people until they testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, establish prayer, and give the obligatory alms. When they do so, they have protected their blood and property from me, except by Islam's right, and their reckoning rests with God.”

segments.arabic: حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد المسندي قال حدثنا أبو روح الحرمي بن عمارة قال حدثنا شعبة عن واقد بن محمد قال سمعت أبي يحدث عن بن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

records.english: On account of the statement of God تعالى, “That is the Garden you have been made to inherit because of what you used to do.” A number of people of knowledge said concerning His statement, تعالى, “By your Lord, We shall surely question them all about what they used to do”: “About saying, ‘There is no god but God.’” And He said, “For the like of this let those who work do their work.”)

records.english: Ahmad ibn Yunus and Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; they both said: Ibrahim ibn Sad narrated to us; he said: Ibn Shihab narrated to us, from Said ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم was asked, “Which deed is best?” He said, “Faith in God and His Messenger.” He was asked, “Then what?” He said, “Striving in God's way.” He was asked, “Then what?” He said, “An accepted pilgrimage.”

records.arabic: حدثنا أبو اليمان قال أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال أخبرني عامر بن سعد بن أبي وقاص عن سعد رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أعطى رهطا وسعد جالس فترك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا هو أعجبهم إلي فقلت يا رسول الله مالك عن فلان فوالله إني لأراه مؤمنا فقال أو مسلما فسكت قليلا ثم غلبني ما أعلم منه فعدت لمقالتي فقلت مالك عن فلان فوالله إني لأراه مؤمنا فقال أو مسلما ثم غلبني ما أعلم منه فعدت لمقالتي وعاد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم قال يا سعد إني لأعطي الرجل وغيره أحب إلي منه خشية أن يكبه الله في النار ورواه يونس وصالح ومعمر وبن أخي الزهري عن الزهري
records.english: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; he said: Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Amir ibn Sad ibn Abi Waqqas informed me, from Sad رضي الله عنه: The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم gave to a group while Sad was sitting there, but the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم left out a man who was the most pleasing of them to me. I said, “Messenger of God, why have you left out so-and-so? By God, I certainly regard him as a believer.” He said, “Or a Muslim.” I remained silent for a little while, but what I knew of him overcame me, so I repeated my statement, saying, “Why have you left out so-and-so? By God, I certainly regard him as a believer.” He said, “Or a Muslim.” Then what I knew of him overcame me, so I repeated my statement, and the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم repeated his response. Then he said, “Sad, I give to a man while another is dearer to me than he, for fear that God might cast him face down into the Fire.” Yunus, Salih, Mamar, and the nephew of al-Zuhri also related it from al-Zuhri.

records.english: Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “I was shown the Fire, and most of its inhabitants were women: they are ungrateful.” It was asked, “Do they disbelieve in God?” He said, “They are ungrateful to their husbands and ungrateful for kindness. If you were good to one of them for all time and then she saw something from you, she would say, ‘I have never seen any good from you at all.’”

records.arabic: حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال حدثنا شعبة عن واصل الأحدب عن المعرور قال لقيت أبا ذر بالربذة وعليه حلة وعلى غلامه حلة فسألته عن ذلك فقال إني ساببت رجلا فعيرته بأمه فقال لي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أبا ذر أعيرته بأمه إنك امرؤ فيك جاهلية إخوانكم خولكم جعلهم الله تحت أيديكم فمن كان أخوه تحت يده فليطعمه مما يأكل وليلبسه مما يلبس ولا تكلفوهم ما يغلبهم فإن كلفتموهم فأعينوهم
records.english: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us; he said: Shubah narrated to us, from Wasil al-Ahdab, from al-Marur, who said: I met Abu Dharr at al-Rabadhah. He wore a suit of clothing, and his slave boy wore a suit of clothing. I asked him about that. He said, “I exchanged insults with a man and taunted him about his mother. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said to me, ‘Abu Dharr, did you taunt him about his mother? You are a man in whom there is ignorance. Your servants are your brothers; God has placed them under your hands. Whoever has his brother under his hand must feed him from what he eats and clothe him from what he wears. Do not burden them with what overcomes them; if you burden them, help them.’”

segments.arabic: حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال حدثنا شعبة عن واصل الأحدب عن المعرور قال لقيت أبا ذر

records.english: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us; Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us; Ayyub and Yunus narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, who said: I went to support this man, and Abu Bakrah met me. He said, “Where are you going?” I said, “To support this man.” He said, “Go back, for I heard the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم say, ‘When two Muslims meet with their swords, both the killer and the one killed are in the Fire.’ I said, ‘Messenger of God, this is the killer, but what of the one killed?’ He said, ‘He was eager to kill his companion.’”

records.arabic: حدثنا قبيصة بن عقبة قال حدثنا سفيان عن الأعمش عن عبد الله بن مرة عن مسروق عن عبد الله بن عمرو أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أربع من كن فيه كان منافقا خالصا ومن كانت فيه خصلة منهن كانت فيه خصلة من النفاق حتى يدعها إذا أؤتمن خان وإذا حدث كذب وإذا عاهد غدر وإذا خاصم فجر تابعه شعبة عن الأعمش
records.english: Qabisah ibn Uqbah narrated to us; he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Amr: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “There are four qualities which, when present in someone, make him an outright hypocrite. Whoever has one of them has a quality of hypocrisy until he abandons it: when entrusted, he betrays the trust; when he speaks, he lies; when he makes a covenant, he acts treacherously; and when he disputes, he acts wickedly.” Shubah followed him in relating it from al-Amash.

قال أربع من كن فيه كان منافقا خالصا ومن كانت فيه خصلة منهن كانت فيه خصلة من النفاق حتى يدعها إذا أؤتمن خان وإذا حدث كذب وإذا عاهد غدر وإذا خاصم فجر

records.english: Harami ibn Hafs narrated to us; he said: Abd al-Wahid narrated to us; he said: Umarah narrated to us; he said: Abu Zurah ibn Amr ibn Jarir narrated to us; he said: I heard Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, who said, “God, عز وجل, has undertaken for whoever goes out in His way—‘Nothing brings him out but faith in Me and affirmation of My messengers—that I return him with the reward or spoils he has obtained, or admit him into the Garden.’ Were it not that I would cause hardship to my community, I would not remain behind any expedition. I wish I could be killed in God's way, then brought to life, then killed, then brought to life, then killed.” [The Arabic moves between third-person reference to God and first-person divine speech; that shift is retained. The inner quotation marks encompass the first-person divine promise; “my community” marks the return to the Prophet’s own voice. These quotation boundaries are editorial.]

records.english: Abd al-Salam ibn Mutahhar narrated to us; he said: Umar ibn Ali narrated to us, from Man ibn Muhammad al-Ghifari, from Said ibn Abi Said al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, who said, “Religion is ease. No one makes religion a contest of severity without its overcoming him. So aim rightly, come close, and take heart. Seek help in the early morning, the latter part of the day, and a little of the night journey.”

records.arabic: حدثنا عمرو بن خالد قال حدثنا زهير قال حدثنا أبو إسحاق عن البراء أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان أول ما قدم المدينة نزل على أجداده أو قال أخواله من الأنصار وأنه صلى قبل بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا أو سبعة عشر شهرا وكان يعجبه أن تكون قبلته قبل البيت وأنه صلى أول صلاة صلاها صلاة العصر وصلى معه قوم فخرج رجل ممن صلى معه فمر على أهل مسجد وهم راكعون فقال أشهد بالله لقد صليت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل مكة فداروا كما هم قبل البيت وكانت اليهود قد أعجبهم إذ كان يصلي قبل بيت المقدس وأهل الكتاب فلما ولى وجهه قبل البيت أنكروا ذلك قال زهير حدثنا أبو إسحاق عن البراء في حديثه هذا أنه مات على القبلة قبل أن تحول رجال وقتلوا فلم ندر ما نقول فيهم فأنزل الله تعالى وما كان الله ليضيع إيمانكم
records.english: Amr ibn Khalid narrated to us; he said: Zuhayr narrated to us; he said: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Bara: When the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم first arrived in Medina, he stayed with his grandfathers—or he said, his maternal uncles—of the Ansar. He prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen months or seventeen months, and he liked the prospect of his direction of prayer being toward the House. The first prayer he prayed [in that direction] was the afternoon prayer, and some people prayed with him. A man who had prayed with him went out and passed people in a mosque while they were bowing. He said, “I testify by God that I have prayed with the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم toward Mecca.” They turned, as they were, toward the House. The Jews had been pleased when he prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis, as had the People of the Book; when he turned his face toward the House, they disapproved of that. Zuhayr said: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Bara, in this report of his, that men had died facing the former direction of prayer before it was changed, and others had been killed. We did not know what to say about them, so God تعالى revealed, “God would not let your faith go to waste.” [The narrator's alternatives about the relatives and the number of months remain unresolved.]

segments.arabic: حدثنا عمرو بن خالد قال حدثنا زهير قال حدثنا أبو إسحاق عن البراء

أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان أول ما قدم المدينة نزل على أجداده أو قال أخواله من الأنصار وأنه صلى قبل بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا أو سبعة عشر شهرا وكان يعجبه أن تكون قبلته قبل البيت وأنه صلى أول صلاة صلاها صلاة العصر وصلى معه قوم فخرج رجل ممن صلى معه فمر على أهل مسجد وهم راكعون فقال أشهد بالله لقد صليت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل مكة فداروا كما هم قبل البيت وكانت اليهود قد أعجبهم إذ كان يصلي قبل بيت المقدس وأهل الكتاب فلما ولى وجهه قبل البيت أنكروا ذلك
قال زهير حدثنا أبو إسحاق عن البراء
في حديثه هذا أنه مات على القبلة قبل أن تحول رجال وقتلوا فلم ندر ما نقول فيهم فأنزل الله تعالى وما كان الله ليضيع إيمانكم

uncertainties.summary: The account gives two alternatives for the relatives with whom the Prophet stayed: grandfathers or maternal uncles. Neither is selected as established genealogy.
The narrator supplies both sixteen months and seventeen months for the earlier direction of prayer. The translation retains both durations.

The appended Zuhayr statement repeats Abu Ishaq and al-Bara but prints no compiler-to-Zuhayr route for that appended occurrence. Its suspension is retained. Grandfathers or maternal uncles and sixteen or seventeen months remain the narrator's alternatives, not resolved genealogy or chronology.

records.english: Malik said: Zayd ibn Aslam informed me that Ata ibn Yasar informed him that Abu Said al-Khudri informed him that he heard the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم say, “When a servant embraces Islam and his Islam becomes good, God expiates for him every evil deed he had previously committed. After that comes the accounting: a good deed receives ten times its like, up to seven hundred times, and an evil deed receives its like, unless God overlooks it.” [Source layout marker: backslash, 1, backslash.]

segments.arabic: قال مالك أخبرني زيد بن أسلم أن عطاء بن يسار أخبره أن أبا سعيد الخدري أخبره أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
يقول إذا أسلم العبد فحسن إسلامه يكفر الله عنه كل سيئة كان زلفها وكان بعد ذلك القصاص الحسنة بعشر أمثالها إلى سبعمائة ضعف والسيئة بمثلها إلا أن يتجاوز الله عنها

records.arabic: حدثنا محمد بن المثنى حدثنا يحيى عن هشام قال أخبرني أبي عن عائشة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دخل عليها وعندها امرأة قال من هذه قالت فلانة تذكر من صلاتها قال مه عليكم بما تطيقون فوالله لا يمل الله حتى تملوا وكان أحب الدين إليه ما داوم عليه صاحبه
records.english: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Hisham, who said: My father informed me, from Aishah: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم entered upon her while a woman was with her. He said, “Who is this?” She said, “So-and-so,” mentioning her prayer. He said, “Enough! Keep to what you can manage. By God, God does not tire until you tire.” The religious practice dearest to him was that which its practitioner maintained. [The final pronoun is retained without deciding whether “him” refers to God or to the Prophet.]

records.english: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; he said: Hisham narrated to us; he said: Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, who said, “Whoever says, ‘There is no god but God,’ and has in his heart a barley grain's weight of goodness will come out of the Fire. Whoever says, ‘There is no god but God,’ and has in his heart a wheat grain's weight of goodness will come out of the Fire. Whoever says, ‘There is no god but God,’ and has in his heart a tiny particle's weight of goodness will come out of the Fire.” Abu Abdullah said: Aban said: Qatadah narrated to us; Anas narrated to us, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, with “of faith” in place of “of goodness.”

records.arabic: حدثنا الحسن بن الصباح سمع جعفر بن عون حدثنا أبو العميس أخبرنا قيس بن مسلم عن طارق بن شهاب عن عمر بن الخطاب أن رجلا من اليهود قال له يا أمير المؤمنين آية في كتابكم تقرؤونها لو علينا معشر اليهود نزلت لاتخذنا ذلك اليوم عيدا قال أي آية قال اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم وأتممت عليكم نعمتي ورضيت لكم الإسلام دينا قال عمر قد عرفنا ذلك اليوم والمكان الذي نزلت فيه على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو قائم بعرفة يوم جمعة
records.english: al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us; he heard Jafar ibn Awn: Abu al-Umays narrated to us: Qays ibn Muslim informed us, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from Umar ibn al-Khattab: A man of the Jews said to him, “Commander of the Believers, there is a verse in your Book that you recite. Had it been sent down to us Jews, we would have made that day a festival.” He said, “Which verse?” He said, “‘Today I have completed your religion for you, fulfilled My favor upon you, and approved Islam as your religion.’” Umar said, “We know that day and the place in which it was sent down upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم: he was standing at Arafah on a Friday.” [The successive colons represent the successive transmission verbs: al-Hasan heard Jafar, Jafar reports Abu al-Umays, and Abu al-Umays reports Qays. The source supplies no intervening “he said” clauses.]

records.arabic: حدثنا إسماعيل قال حدثني مالك بن أنس عن عمه أبي سهيل بن مالك عن أبيه أنه سمع طلحة بن عبيد الله يقول جاء رجل إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أهل نجد ثائر الرأس يسمع دوي صوته ولا يفقه ما يقول حتى دنا فإذا هو يسأل عن الإسلام فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خمس صلوات في اليوم والليلة فقال هل علي غيرها قال لا إلا أن تطوع قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وصيام رمضان قال هل علي غيره قال لا إلا أن تطوع قال وذكر له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الزكاة قال هل علي غيرها قال لا إلا أن تطوع قال فأدبر الرجل وهو يقول والله لا أزيد على هذا ولا أنقص قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أفلح إن صدق
records.english: Ismail narrated to us; he said: Malik ibn Anas narrated to me, from his uncle Abu Suhayl ibn Malik, from his father, that he heard Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah say: A man from Najd came to the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم, his hair disheveled. The sound of his voice could be heard, but what he was saying could not be understood, until he came near. He was asking about Islam. The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “Five prayers in the day and night.” He said, “Am I obliged to do any others?” He said, “No, unless you do so voluntarily.” The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “And fasting Ramadan.” He said, “Am I obliged to do any other fasting?” He said, “No, unless you do so voluntarily.” He related: The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم mentioned the obligatory alms to him. He said, “Am I obliged to give anything else?” He said, “No, unless you do so voluntarily.” He related: The man turned away saying, “By God, I will neither add to this nor take away from it.” The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “He has prospered, if he is truthful.”

records.arabic: حدثنا أحمد بن عبد الله بن علي المنجوفي قال حدثنا روح قال حدثنا عوف عن الحسن ومحمد عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من اتبع جنازة مسلم إيمانا واحتسابا وكان معه حتى يصلي عليها ويفرغ من دفنها فإنه يرجع من الأجر بقيراطين كل قيراط مثل أحد ومن صلى عليها ثم رجع قبل أن تدفن فإنه يرجع بقيراط تابعه عثمان المؤذن قال حدثنا عوف عن محمد عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نحوه
records.english: Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ali al-Manjufi narrated to us; he said: Rawh narrated to us; he said: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan and Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “Whoever follows a Muslim's funeral with faith and seeking reward, remaining with it until he prays over it and its burial is finished, returns with two qirats of reward, each qirat like Uhud. Whoever prays over it and then returns before it is buried returns with one qirat.” Uthman al-Muadhdhin followed him in relating it; he said: Awf narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, something similar.

records.arabic: وقال إبراهيم التيمي ما عرضت قولي على عملي إلا خشيت أن أكون مكذبا وقال بن أبي مليكة أدركت ثلاثين من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كلهم يخاف النفاق على نفسه ما منهم أحد يقول إنه علي إيمان جبريل وميكائيل ويذكر عن الحسن ما خافه إلا مؤمن ولا أمنه إلا منافق وما يحذر من الإصرار على النفاق والعصيان من غير توبة لقول الله تعالى ولم يصروا على ما فعلوا وهم يعلمون )
records.english: Ibrahim al-Taymi said, “Whenever I have set my speech against my action, I have feared being one who is belied.” [“One who is belied” reads the unvocalized “مكذبا” in the context of testing speech against action: the action may belie the speech. No source vowel marks are supplied.] Ibn Abi Mulaykah said, “I met thirty of the companions of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. All of them feared hypocrisy for themselves; none of them said that he was upon the faith of Jibril and Mikail.” It is related from al-Hasan: “Only a believer fears it, and only a hypocrite feels safe from it.” And the warning against persisting in hypocrisy and disobedience without repentance, on account of the statement of God تعالى, “They did not knowingly persist in what they had done.”) [The supplied spelling is “علي”; “upon” is the contextual reading corresponding to “على”, without changing the Arabic.]

Ibn Abi Mulaykah says he met thirty companions but no compiler route to him is printed. Those thirty are the subjects of his observation, not thirty invented chain nodes; Jibril and Mikail likewise belong to his quoted comparison.

It is related from al-Hasan is an explicitly non-specific attribution. The gap and suspended mode preserve the absent compiler route; the source-local al-Hasan identity is not joined to other identical spellings without evidence.

records.english: Qutaybah ibn Said informed us; Ismail ibn Jafar narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: Ubadah ibn al-Samit informed me that the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم came out to tell of the Night of Decree, but two Muslim men quarreled. He said, “I came out to tell you of the Night of Decree, but so-and-so and so-and-so quarreled, and it was taken away. Perhaps that will be better for you. Seek it in the seventh, the ninth, and the fifth.” [The source does not specify here how these numbered nights are counted.] [The object of “it was taken away” is implicit; its connection to disclosure of the Night is a contextual inference, not an explicitly named object.]

records.english: (36. Chapter: Jibril's asking the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم about faith, Islam, excellence, and knowledge of the Hour, and the explanation the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم gave him. Then he said, “Jibril عليه السلام came to teach you your religion.” Thus he made all of that religion. And what the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم explained to the delegation of Abd al-Qays concerning faith; and His statement, تعالى, “Whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him.”)

records.arabic: حدثنا مسدد قال حدثنا إسماعيل بن إبراهيم أخبرنا أبو حيان التيمي عن أبي زرعة عن أبي هريرة قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بارزا يوما للناس فأتاه جبريل فقال ما الإيمان قال أن تؤمن بالله وملائكته وبلقائه ورسله وتؤمن بالبعث قال ما الإسلام قال الإسلام أن تعبد الله ولا تشرك به وتقيم الصلاة وتؤدي الزكاة المفروضة وتصوم رمضان قال ما الإحسان قال أن تعبد الله كأنك تراه فإن لم تكن تراه فإنه يراك قال متى الساعة قال ما المسؤول عنها بأعلم من السائل وسأخبرك عن أشراطها إذا ولدت الأمة ربها وإذا تطاول رعاة الإبل البهم في البنيان في خمس لا يعلمهن إلا الله ثم تلا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله عنده علم الساعة الآية ثم أدبر فقال ردوه فلم يروا شيئا فقال هذا جبريل جاء يعلم الناس دينهم قال أبو عبد الله جعل ذلك كله من الإيمان
records.english: Musaddad narrated to us; he said: Ismail ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; Abu Hayyan al-Taymi informed us, from Abu Zurah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: One day the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم was out before the people when Jibril came to him and said, “What is faith?” He said, “That you believe in God, His angels, meeting Him, and His messengers, and believe in resurrection.” He said, “What is Islam?” He said, “Islam is that you worship God, associate nothing with Him, establish prayer, pay the prescribed obligatory alms, and fast Ramadan.” He said, “What is excellence?” He said, “That you worship God as though you see Him; if you do not see Him, He sees you.” He said, “When is the Hour?” He said, “The one asked about it knows no more than the questioner. I shall tell you about its signs: when the slave woman gives birth to her master, and when the herders of black camels compete in building tall buildings. Among five things that none knows except God.” Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم recited, “God has knowledge of the Hour”—the verse. Then he turned away. He said, “Bring him back.” But they saw nothing. He said, “This is Jibril; he came to teach people their religion.” Abu Abdullah said, “He made all of that part of faith.” [The unvocalized “البهم” is read here as describing black camels; a reading describing the herders’ condition remains possible, and the transcription does not settle the attachment or vocalization. The compressed “among five” is contextually connected to knowledge of the Hour, not a statement that the preceding signs are the five. The subject is not restated, and the five are not enumerated here.]

records.english: Ibrahim ibn Hamzah narrated to us; he said: Ibrahim ibn Sad narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah: Abdullah ibn Abbas informed him, saying: Abu Sufyan informed me that Heraclius said to him, “I asked you whether they increase or decrease, and you stated that they increase. So it is with faith until it becomes complete. I asked you whether anyone renounces it out of displeasure with his religion after entering it, and you stated that no one does. So it is with faith: when its delight mingles with hearts, no one is displeased with it.”

records.arabic: حدثنا أبو نعيم حدثنا زكرياء عن عامر قال سمعت النعمان بن بشير يقول سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول الحلال بين والحرام بين وبينهما مشبهات لا يعلمها كثير من الناس فمن اتقي المشبهات استبرأ لدينه وعرضه ومن وقع في الشبهات كراع يرعى حول الحمى يوشك أن يواقعه ألا وإن لكل ملك حمى ألا إن حمى الله في أرضه محارمه ألا وإن في الجسد مضغة إذا صلحت صلح الجسد كله وإذا فسدت فسد الجسد كله ألا وهي القلب
records.english: Abu Nuaym narrated to us; Zakariyya narrated to us, from Amir, who said: I heard al-Numan ibn Bashir say: I heard the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم say, “The lawful is clear, and the unlawful is clear. Between them are doubtful matters which many people do not know. Whoever guards against doubtful matters safeguards his religion and honor. Whoever falls into doubtful matters is like a shepherd grazing around a protected reserve, on the point of entering it. Indeed, every king has a protected reserve. Indeed, God's protected reserve on His earth is what He has forbidden. Indeed, in the body is a morsel of flesh: when it is sound, the whole body is sound, and when it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart.”

records.arabic: حدثنا علي بن الجعد قال أخبرنا شعبة عن أبي جمرة قال كنت أقعد مع بن عباس يجلسني على سريره فقال أقم عندي حتى أجعل لك سهما من مالي فأقمت معه شهرين ثم قال إن وفد عبد القيس لما أتوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من القوم أو من الوفد قالوا ربيعة قال مرحبا بالقوم أو بالوفد غير خزايا ولا ندامى فقالوا يا رسول الله إنا لا نستطيع أن نأتيك إلا في شهر الحرام وبيننا وبينك هذا الحي من كفار مضر فمرنا بأمر فصل نخبر به من وراءنا وندخل به الجنة وسألوه عن الأشربة فأمرهم بأربع ونهاهم عن أربع أمرهم بالإيمان بالله وحده قال أتدرون ما الإيمان بالله وحده قالوا الله ورسوله أعلم قال شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وصيام رمضان وأن تعطوا من المغنم الخمس ونهاهم عن أربع عن الحنتم والدباء والنقير والمزفت وربما قال المقير وقال احفظوهن وأخبروا بهن من وراءكم \ 1 \
records.english: Ali ibn al-Jad narrated to us; he said: Shubah informed us, from Abu Jamrah, who said: I used to sit with Ibn Abbas; he would seat me on his couch. He said, “Stay with me so that I may assign you a share of my property.” I stayed with him for two months. Then he said: When the delegation of Abd al-Qays came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, he said, “Who are the people—or the delegation?” They said, “Rabiah.” He said, “Welcome to the people—or the delegation—neither disgraced nor regretful.” They said, “Messenger of God, we can come to you only in the sacred month. Between us and you is this group of the unbelievers of Mudar. Command us with a decisive command that we may convey to those behind us and through which we may enter the Garden.” They asked him about drinks. He commanded them to do four things and forbade them four things. He commanded them to believe in God alone. He said, “Do you know what faith in God alone is?” They said, “God and His Messenger know best.” He said, “Testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God; establishing prayer; giving the obligatory alms; fasting Ramadan; and giving the fifth of the spoils.” He forbade them four things: glazed jars, gourds, hollowed-out trunks, and pitch-coated vessels. Sometimes he said, “tar-coated vessels.” He said, “Keep these in mind and tell those behind you.” [The alternatives and the source's count of four alongside the ensuing enumeration are retained.] [Source layout marker: backslash, 1, backslash.]

records.arabic: ( 39 باب ما جاء أن الأعمال بالنية والحسبة ولكل امرئ ما نوى فدخل فيه الإيمان والوضوء والصلاة والزكاة والحج والصوم والأحكام وقال الله تعالى قل كل يعمل على شاكلته على نيته نفقة الرجل على أهله يحتسبها صدقة وقال ولكن جهاد ونية )
records.english: (39. Chapter: What has been related that deeds depend on intention and seeking reward, and each person has what he intended. This includes faith, ablution, prayer, obligatory alms, pilgrimage, fasting, and legal judgments. God تعالى said, “Say: Each acts according to his disposition”—according to his intention. A man's spending on his family, seeking reward for it, is charity. And he said, “But striving and intention.” [The source does not explicitly name the speaker of this final quotation here.])

records.arabic: حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة قال أخبرنا مالك عن يحيى بن سعيد عن محمد بن إبراهيم عن علقمة بن وقاص عن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال الأعمال بالنية ولكل امرئ ما نوى فمن كانت هجرته إلى الله ورسوله فهجرته إلى الله ورسوله ومن كانت هجرته لدنيا يصيبها أو امرأة يتزوجها فهجرته إلى ما هاجر إليه
records.english: Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us; he said: Malik informed us, from Yahya ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Alqamah ibn Waqqas, from Umar: The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “Deeds depend on intention, and each person has what he intended. Whoever's emigration was to God and His Messenger, his emigration is to God and His Messenger. Whoever's emigration was for worldly gain he would obtain or a woman he would marry, his emigration is to that for which he emigrated.”

segments.arabic: حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة قال أخبرنا مالك عن يحيى بن سعيد عن محمد بن إبراهيم عن علقمة بن وقاص عن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

records.arabic: حدثنا أبو النعمان قال حدثنا أبو عوانة عن زياد بن علاقة قال سمعت جرير بن عبد الله يقول يوم مات المغيرة بن شعبة قام فحمد الله وأثنى عليه وقال عليكم باتقاء الله وحده لا شريك له والوقار والسكينة حتى يأتيكم أمير فإنما يأتيكم الآن ثم قال استعفوا لأميركم فإنه كان يحب العفو ثم قال أما بعد فإني أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قلت أبايعك على الإسلام فشرط علي والنصح لكل مسلم فبايعته على هذا ورب هذا المسجد إني لناصح لكم ثم استغفر ونزل 5 بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
records.english: Abu al-Numan narrated to us; he said: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Ilaqah, who said: I heard Jarir ibn Abdullah speaking on the day al-Mughirah ibn Shubah died. He stood, praised God and extolled Him, and said, “You must be reverent toward God alone, who has no partner, and maintain dignity and tranquility until a governor comes to you, for he is only now about to come to you.” Then he said, “Ask pardon for your governor, for he loved pardon.” Then he said, “To proceed: I came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and said, ‘I pledge to you upon Islam.’ He stipulated for me, ‘And sincerity toward every Muslim.’ So I pledged to him on this basis. By the Lord of this mosque, I am sincere toward you.” Then he asked forgiveness and came down. [Source layout/transition, outside Jarir's narration: terminal number 5; “بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم”]

records.arabic: حدثنا محمد بن سنان قال حدثنا فليح ح وحدثني إبراهيم بن المنذر قال حدثنا محمد بن فليح قال حدثني أبي قال حدثني هلال بن علي عن عطاء بن يسار عن أبي هريرة قال بينما النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في مجلس يحدث القوم جاءه أعرابي فقال متى الساعة فمضى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يحدث فقال بعض القوم سمع ما قال فكره ما قال وقال بعضهم بل لم يسمع حتى إذا قضى حديثه قال أين أراه السائل عن الساعة قال ها أنا يا رسول الله قال فإذا ضيعت الأمانة فانتظر الساعة قال كيف إضاعتها قال إذا وسد الأمر إلى غير أهله فانتظر الساعة
records.english: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Fulayh narrated to us. [Change of chain.] And Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Fulayh narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: Hilal ibn Ali narrated to me, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: While the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم was in a gathering speaking to the people, a desert Arab came to him and said, "When is the Hour?" the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم continued speaking. Some of the people said, "He heard what he said and disliked it." Others said, "Rather, he did not hear." When he finished his discourse, he said, "Where is—I think he said—the one asking about the Hour?" He said to the Messenger of God, "Here I am." He said, "When trust is squandered, expect the Hour." He said, "How is it squandered?" He said, "When authority is entrusted to those unfit for it, expect the Hour."

He caught up with us when the prayer had become pressing upon us and we were performing ablution. We began wiping our feet. He called out at the top of his voice, "Woe to the heels from the Fire!" twice or three times.

records.arabic: وقال لنا الحميدي كان عند بن عيينة حدثنا وأخبرنا وأنبأنا وسمعت واحدا وقال بن مسعود حدثنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو الصادق المصدوق وقال شقيق عن عبد الله سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كلمة وقال حذيفة حدثنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حديثين وقال أبو العالية عن بن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما يروى عن ربه وقال أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يرويه عن ربه عز وجل وقال أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يرويه عن ربكم عز وجل )
records.english: al-Humaydi said to us: Ibn Uyaynah regarded "He narrated to us," "He informed us," "He told us," and "I heard" as one. Ibn Masud said: the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم narrated to us, and he is truthful and believed. Shaqiq said, from Abdullah: I heard the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم say a word. Hudhayfah said: the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم narrated two reports to us. Abu al-Aliyah said, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, concerning what he relates from his Lord. Anas said, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, relating it from his Lord عز وجل. Abu Hurayrah said, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, relating it from your Lord عز وجل.

records.arabic: حدثنا قتيبة حدثنا إسماعيل بن جعفر عن عبد الله بن دينار عن بن عمر قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن من الشجر شجرة لا يسقط ورقها وإنها مثل المسلم فحدثوني ما هي فوقع الناس في شجر البوادي قال عبد الله ووقع في نفسي أنها النخلة فاستحييت ثم قالوا حدثنا ما هي يا رسول الله قال هي النخلة
records.english: Qutaybah narrated to us: Ismail ibn Jafar narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar, who said: the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said, "Among trees there is a tree whose leaves do not fall, and it is like the Muslim. Tell me what it is." The people turned their thoughts to the trees of the wilderness. Abdullah said: It occurred to me that it was the date palm, but I felt shy. Then they said to the Messenger of God, "Tell us what it is." He said, "It is the date palm."

records.arabic: القراءة والعرض على المحدث ورأى الحسن والثوري ومالك القراءة جائزة واحتج بعضهم في القراءة على العالم بحديث ضمام بن ثعلبة قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم آلله أمرك أن نصلي الصلوات قال نعم قال فهذه قراءة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أخبر ضمام قومه بذلك فأجازوه واحتج مالك بالصك يقرأ على القوم فيقولون أشهدنا فلان ويقرأ ذلك قراءة عليهم ويقرأ على المقرئ فيقول القارئ أقرأني فلان حدثنا محمد بن سلام حدثنا محمد بن الحسن الواسطي عن عوف عن الحسن قال لا بأس بالقراءة على العالم وحدثنا عبيد الله بن موسى عن سفيان قال إذا قرئ على المحدث فلا بأس أن يقول حدثني قال وسمعت أبا عاصم يقول عن مالك وسفيان القراءة على العالم وقراءته سواء )
records.english: Reading and presenting a text to a transmitter. al-Hasan, al-Thawri, and Malik considered reading permissible. Some of them argued for reading to a scholar using the report of Dimam ibn Thalabah: he said to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, "Did God command you that we should perform the prayers?" He said, "Yes." He said: This is a reading to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. Dimam informed his people of it, and they accepted it. Malik argued from a document read to people, who then say, "So-and-so called us as witnesses," though it is read aloud to them; and from reading to a recitation teacher, after which the reader says, "So-and-so taught me to recite." Muhammad ibn Salam narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Wasiti narrated to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: There is no harm in reading to a scholar. And Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: When a text is read to a transmitter, there is no harm in saying, "He narrated to me." He said: I heard Abu Asim say, from Malik and Sufyan: Reading to a scholar and his reading are alike.

records.arabic: حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال حدثنا الليث عن سعيد هو المقبري عن شريك بن عبد الله بن أبي نمر أنه سمع أنس بن مالك يقول بينما نحن جلوس مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في المسجد دخل رجل على جمل فأناخه في المسجد ثم عقله ثم قال لهم أيكم محمد والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم متكئ بين ظهرانيهم فقلنا هذا الرجل الأبيض المتكئ فقال له الرجل بن عبد المطلب فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد أجبتك فقال الرجل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إني سائلك فمشدد عليك في المسألة فلا تجد علي في نفسك فقال سل عما بدا لك فقال أسألك بربك ورب من قبلك آلله أرسلك إلى الناس كلهم فقال اللهم نعم قال أنشدك بالله آلله أمرك أن نصلي الصلوات الخمس في اليوم والليلة قال اللهم نعم قال أنشدك بالله آلله أمرك أن نصوم هذا الشهر من السنة قال اللهم نعم قال أنشدك بالله آلله أمرك أن تأخذ هذه الصدقة من أغنيائنا فتقسمها على فقرائنا فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اللهم نعم فقال الرجل آمنت بما جئت به وأنا رسول من ورائي من قومي وأنا ضمام بن ثعلبة أخو بني سعد بن بكر رواه موسى وعلي بن عبد الحميد عن سليمان عن ثابت عن أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بهذا
records.english: Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to us, from Said, that is, al-Maqburi, from Sharik ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Namir, that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: While we were sitting with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم in the mosque, a man entered on a camel. He made it kneel in the mosque, then tethered it, then said to them, "Which of you is Muhammad?" the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم was reclining among them. We said, "This fair man who is reclining." The man said to him, "Ibn Abd al-Muttalib?" the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said to him, "I have answered you." The man said to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, "I am going to question you and will be forceful in questioning you, so do not resent me inwardly." He said, "Ask whatever occurs to you." He said, "I ask you by your Lord and the Lord of those before you: did God send you to all people?" He said, "اللهم yes." He said, "I adjure you by God: did God command you that we should perform the five prayers during the day and night?" He said, "اللهم yes." He said, "I adjure you by God: did God command you that we should fast this month of the year?" He said, "اللهم yes." He said, "I adjure you by God: did God command you to take this charity from our rich and distribute it among our poor?" the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said, "اللهم yes." The man said, "I believe in what you have brought. I am the emissary of my people whom I left behind, and I am Dimam ibn Thalabah, a brother of Banu Sad ibn Bakr." Musa and Ali ibn Abd al-Hamid related it, from Sulayman, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, to this effect.

records.english: Anas said: Uthman copied the written copies of the Quran and sent them to the regions. Abdullah ibn Umar, Yahya ibn Said, and Malik considered that permissible. Some of the people of al-Hijaz argued for handing over a text using the report of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, when he wrote a letter for the commander of a detachment and said, "Do not read it until you reach such-and-such a place." When he reached that place, he read it to the people and informed them of the command of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم.

records.english: Ismail ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sad narrated to me, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Masud, that Abdullah ibn Abbas informed him that the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم sent a man with his letter and ordered him to hand it to the ruler of al-Bahrayn. The ruler of al-Bahrayn handed it to Kisra. When he read it, he tore it up. I think that Ibn al-Musayyab said: the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم prayed against them that they should be torn utterly apart. [Source layout marker: \ 1 \]

records.arabic: حدثنا محمد بن مقاتل أبو الحسن أخبرنا عبد الله قال أخبرنا شعبة عن قتادة عن أنس بن مالك قال كتب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كتابا أو أراد أن يكتب فقيل له إنهم لا يقرؤون كتابا إلا مختوما فاتخذ خاتما من فضة نقشه محمد رسول الله كأني أنظر إلى بياضه في يده فقلت لقتادة من قال نقشه محمد رسول الله قال أنس
records.english: Muhammad ibn Muqatil Abu al-Hasan narrated to us: Abdullah informed us, saying: Shubah informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم wrote a letter—or wanted to write—and was told, "They do not read a letter unless it is sealed." So he took a silver ring, whose inscription was "Muhammad the Messenger of God." It is as though I can see its whiteness on his hand. I said to Qatadah, "Who said that its inscription was 'Muhammad the Messenger of God'?" He said, "Anas."
